comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that IPC activity depends on nutritional state, with starvation silencing IPCs. OpenEval R1 covers broader claim set (C3-C52, C154) including detailed temporal dynamics, while Peer R1 focuses on subset (C3-C48). Both cite reviewer praise for 'convincing' and 'excellent' electrophysiological evidence.

Substantial overlap on temporal dynamics claims (C49-C52, C154-C156). Both support slow recovery kinetics after glucose feeding. Peer R2 explicitly notes 'compelling' evidence for slow time course, while OpenEval R1 includes this within broader nutritional state modulation analysis.

Both support sugar-specific IPC responses (C5-C7, C55-C57). OpenEval R2 notes puzzling lack of standard diet response and cites appropriate controls. Peer R3 affirms 'compelling' evidence for nutritive sugar specificity. Both treat findings as well-supported despite some interpretive questions.

Minimal overlap (C58-C59). Both accept observations about standard diet and high protein diet effects on IPCs. OpenEval R2 questions biological significance, while Peer R4 accepts without challenge. Speculative interpretations about insulin sensitivity acknowledged as discussion points.

Both address lack of direct glucose sensing by IPCs (C8, C103-C106). OpenEval R3 rates as UNCERTAIN due to alternative explanations and methodological concerns, while Peer R5 rates as SUPPORTED with all reviewers explicitly affirming 'compelling evidence.' Major concordance disagreement on confidence level despite agreeing on the negative perfusion result.

Both address incretin-like interpretation (C9, C107, C170-C172, C174-C175). OpenEval R3 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation and need for additional experiments. Peer R6 rates as SUPPORTED with all reviewers explicitly endorsing incretin mechanism. Significant concordance disagreement on whether indirect evidence sufficiently supports incretin interpretation.

Strong agreement on DH44PIN glucose sensitivity (C10, C109, C111-C115, C119-C124). Both rate as SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical validation. OpenEval R4 provides detailed electrophysiological analysis, Peer R7 affirms findings without objection and notes validation that negative IPC result was not artifactual.

Partial overlap on DH44PIN characterization (C116-C118, C188-C189). Both support nutritional state-dependent firing patterns and glucose sensitivity. OpenEval R4 notes ISI analysis suggests modulation beyond rate changes, Peer R8 accepts detailed characterizations as part of 'convincing' electrophysiological analysis.

Perfect claim overlap (C11, C135-C138) on DH44PIN-IPC functional independence. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R5 emphasizes contrast with broad line effects and proper controls. Peer R9 accepts as 'useful data' distinguishing DH44 neuron populations. Complete concordance.

Strong overlap on DH44N inhibition of IPCs (C12, C125-C132). Both rate as SUPPORTED with robust electrophysiological evidence. OpenEval R6 notes uncertainty about inhibitory neuron identity (LK+ vs non-DH44 neurons). Peer R10 accepts as 'useful data' without addressing identity questions. Agreement on phenomenon, divergence on mechanistic certainty.

Minimal overlap (C138 only). Both support conclusion about functional independence and parallel pathways. OpenEval R5 focuses on negative optogenetic result, Peer R11 emphasizes integrative conclusion about multiple interacting neuronal layers. Complementary perspectives on same conceptual framework.

Perfect claim overlap (C14-C15, C80-C91) on IPC optogenetic effects on locomotion. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R7 emphasizes small effect sizes, transient nature, and confounds. Peer R14 accepts findings as 'compelling' evidence for negligible IPC contribution to hyperactivity. Agreement on data, slight difference in emphasis on limitations.

High overlap (C16, C94-C101) on OAN behavioral effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R8 notes strong effects but questions stopping behavior interpretation as speculative. Peer R15 accepts results without objection as evidence for non-IPC modulatory control. Agreement on findings, OpenEval more cautious on mechanistic interpretation.

Minimal overlap (C102 only). Both support conclusion that multiple modulatory systems control starvation-induced hyperactivity beyond IPCs. OpenEval R8 derives this from OAN data, Peer R13 explicitly affirms as key insight with 'compelling' evidence. Complete concordance on this integrative conclusion.

Perfect claim overlap (C140-C151) on DH44N behavioral effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R9 notes reciprocal inhibition proposal is 'reasonable but somewhat speculative.' Peer R16 accepts as 'compelling' evidence with 'high quality' optogenetic manipulations. Agreement on data quality, slight difference on mechanistic certainty.

Strong overlap (C69-C75) on nutritional state effects on behavior. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R10 emphasizes complex relationship where glucose refeeding only partially reduces hyperactivity. Peer R12 confirms behavioral data and accepts correlation with IPC activity. Agreement on observations and interpretation of multiple parallel systems.

Partial overlap (C74-C75, C102). Both support conclusion that IPCs make negligible contribution to locomotion modulation. OpenEval R10 derives from refeeding dissociation, Peer R13 explicitly affirms as 'strong evidence' and 'compelling.' Complete concordance on this key negative finding.

Minimal overlap (C76, C79) on temporal dynamics of starvation effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R10 notes similar timescales for IPC and behavioral modulation. Peer R19 accepts detailed temporal characterization without challenge. Agreement on descriptive findings.

Minimal overlap (C53 only) on IPC hyperactivity after prolonged glucose feeding. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R11 questions physiological relevance. Peer R2 accepts as part of 'compelling' temporal dynamics data. Agreement on observation, difference in emphasis on significance.

Minimal overlap (C61 only) on survival data validating diet protocols. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R11 uses survival data to interpret lack of IPC recovery on HP diet. Peer R4 accepts without specific comment. Agreement on validation data.

Perfect overlap (C62-C63) on lack of sex/mating effects. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R12 notes modest sample sizes but clear results. Peer R17 accepts without challenge as adequate control data. Complete concordance.

Perfect overlap (C64-C65, C161-C163) on age-dependent IPC activity reduction. Both rate as SUPPORTED for data, with speculative interpretations about survival mechanisms appropriately framed. OpenEval R12 and Peer R18 both accept observations while noting speculation. Complete concordance.

Strong overlap (C152-C153, C155-C157) on connecting findings to prior DILP accumulation literature and multi-timescale integration. OpenEval R13 rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative insulin sensitivity interpretation. Peer R20 rates as SUPPORTED, accepting connection to molecular studies. Moderate concordance disagreement on whether interpretive framework is sufficiently supported.

Partial overlap (C155-C156) on multi-timescale integration hypothesis. OpenEval R13 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation. Peer R2 accepts temporal dynamics as 'compelling' contribution. Difference reflects OpenEval's caution about mechanistic interpretation vs peer acceptance of descriptive framework.

Strong overlap (C108, C174-C178) on incretin-like mechanism interpretation. OpenEval R14 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting gut neuropeptides are speculative and alternative explanations not fully ruled out. Peer R6 rates as SUPPORTED with all reviewers explicitly endorsing incretin interpretation. Major concordance disagreement on sufficiency of indirect evidence.

Strong overlap (C188-C189, C190-C192) on DH44PIN nutritional state-dependent glucose sensitivity. OpenEval R15 rates as SUPPORTED for data but notes mechanistic explanations (ISI-based release, change detection) are speculative. Peer R8 accepts characterizations as part of 'convincing' analysis. Agreement on observations, OpenEval more cautious on mechanisms.

Minimal overlap (C179 only) on synthesis of distinct IPC vs DH44PIN responses. Both support conclusion about complementary roles in parallel pathways. OpenEval R15 emphasizes mechanistic uncertainty, Peer R11 emphasizes conceptual advance. Agreement on integrative framework.

Partial overlap (C181-C187) on DH44N-IPC connectivity mechanism. OpenEval R16 rates as UNCERTAIN regarding whether connections are peptidergic vs synaptic and identity of inhibitory neurons. Peer R10 rates as SUPPORTED, accepting inhibitory connections without addressing mechanistic details. Agreement on functional connectivity, divergence on mechanistic certainty.

OpenEval R17 covers extensive background claims (C1-C43) establishing prior literature context. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses background claims as a separate evaluation unit. Peer reviews implicitly accept background as appropriate framing.

Partial overlap (C66-C68, C92-C93) on background claims about starvation-induced hyperactivity and metabolic context. OpenEval R18 rates background as SUPPORTED by citations. Peer R12 confirms 'the data confirm earlier studies that nutritional state strongly affects locomotion.' Agreement on established context.

Minimal overlap (C167-C169, C173) on background claims about incretin systems. OpenEval R18 rates background as SUPPORTED by citations. Peer R6 uses this background to support incretin interpretation of current findings. Agreement on established vertebrate literature.

Strong overlap (C158-C165) on speculative discussion claims about DILP6, protein diet effects, aging mechanisms, and evolutionary conservation. OpenEval R19 rates as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of direct experimental support. Peer R18 rates as SUPPORTED, accepting as appropriate discussion framing. Concordance disagreement reflects different standards for discussion vs results claims.

Minimal overlap (C159-C160) on protein diet speculation based on mammalian studies. OpenEval R19 rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct testing. Peer R4 accepts without challenge as discussion point. Agreement that claims are speculative but appropriate for discussion section.
